name: Rogervoice
oneLine: French app that captions phone calls in real time for deaf and hard of hearing people; since October 2026 it also captions in-person conversations.

platforms.detail: Rogervoice's help centre says the app runs only on iPhone, iPad and Android phones and tablets.

deviceRequirements.text: iOS 16+ or Android 7+; Live captions iOS 26+
deviceRequirements.detail: The app needs iOS 16 or later (iPhone 8 or newer) or Android 7 or later, and a mobile number to sign up. The new Live captions mode needs iOS 26 or later on iPhone; Rogervoice says it works on all Android phones.

roomCaptions.detail: Live captions shows what people around you say in real time, with text size and pause. It arrived in app version 6.1.0 on 26 October 2026, and Rogervoice's official pages say little more about it so far.

groupConversations.detail: No official page says how Live captions handles several people talking, or whether it can use more than one phone or an external microphone.

languages.detail: Rogervoice's international site and US App Store listing say 100+ languages, its French listings say more than 80, and its help-centre list (from 2021) has 119 language and region entries in 64 languages. Languages for Live captions are not stated.

offline.text: Yes, Live captions in airplane mode
offline.detail: Rogervoice's French features page says face-to-face captions work even in airplane mode; its help article doesn't mention it. Phone calls need Wi-Fi or mobile data.

speakerLabels.detail: No official page says Live captions shows who is talking. During calls, a setting can also show your own words as text.

translation.detail: The help centre says Rogervoice does not translate conversations from one language to another; you pick the caption language for each call.

saveTranscripts.detail: Call transcripts can be saved on the phone (a setting you can turn off) and re-read in Recents, and Live captions transcripts can be re-read too. Rogervoice says it keeps no transcripts on its servers; how long the phone keeps them is not stated.

export.detail: Live captions transcripts can be exported, and an app update added exporting conversations to save or share them. The file format is not stated.

fileUpload.detail: No official page mentions transcribing audio or video files.

summaries.detail: No official page mentions AI summaries or notes.

customWords.detail: No official page mentions adding your own words or names.

display.detail: You can change caption size and choose one of 4 appearance themes, including a blue and yellow theme for people with low vision. The store listings also mention dark, light and high-contrast modes.

soundAlerts.detail: No official page mentions alerts for non-speech sounds.

phoneCalls.detail: It captions incoming and outgoing calls word for word, lets you reply by voice or by typing (read out for you), transcribes voicemail and lets you keep your own number. The other person needs nothing, and each call can last up to 2 hours.

videoCalls.detail: Captioned video calls work when both people have the Rogervoice app and you have a subscription or, in the US, FCC registration. Captioning Zoom, Teams or Meet is not stated.

mediaOnDevice.detail: No official page mentions captioning audio or video playing on the phone.

humanCaptioners.text: France only, in the 5 h relay offer
humanCaptioners.detail: In France, the operator-funded relay offer lets you add a human 'copilote' who corrects captions and describes the other person's tone, within 5 hours a month on weekdays 8:30 to 21:00 and Saturday 8:30 to 13:00. Paid plans use automatic captions only.

signLanguage.detail: In France, the operator-funded relay offer includes calls through a qualified French Sign Language (LSF) interpreter by video, a Cued French (LfPC) coder, or a braille-compatible mode, within 5 hours a month and opening hours.

privacy.text: Cloud for calls; no transcripts on servers
privacy.detail: Rogervoice says calls are captioned automatically with no person listening, that it stores no call audio or transcripts on its servers, and that EU users' data stays in Europe. Its French App Store privacy label lists identifiers as data used to track you.

account.detail: You sign up with your phone number and a code sent by SMS. A Rogervoice number in France can need proof of address or ID, and free US service needs FCC registration with a Social Security number.

availability.detail: The help centre lists 44 countries where you can download it, 38 where you can buy a plan or credit, and 9 where you can receive calls, including France, the US, the UK and Canada. Its international site says more than 52 countries.

freePlan.detail: The app is free, calls between Rogervoice users are free, and new users outside the US get 30 free minutes of calls for their first year; free calls in the US and France come through public programmes. Rogervoice doesn't say whether Live captions costs anything.

price.detail: Freedom (a number and 1 hour of calls a month) or Premium (unlimited calls), billed by Apple or Google, October 2026: US$5.99 or US$29.99 (US), €5.99 or €29.99 (France), £5.49 or £27.49 (UK). Extra credit of 2 hours costs €11.99 in France and £9.99 in the UK (US$10.99 in the English help centre), and a French business plan €1,200 a year before VAT.

accessibilityFunding.detail: In the US it is free for eligible users with hearing loss, paid by the FCC (certified since March 2024). In France, under French law, Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom, La Poste Mobile and their brands pay for 5 hours of calls a month since 1 October 2026 (3 hours before, as the French App Store listing still says), and the MDPH and Agefiph can reimburse subscriptions.

strengths.text: Captions phone calls to any number in real time, with typed replies read aloud, voicemail transcription and the option to keep your own number.
Free for eligible US users through the FCC, and 5 hours of calls a month in France through major operators, including LSF interpreters, LfPC coders and human-corrected captions.
A new Live captions mode captions people in the room; its French site says it works in airplane mode, and transcripts can be re-read and exported.
Says it never stores call audio or transcripts on its servers; transcripts stay on the phone.

limits.text: Outside the US, calls to people without the app need a plan or credit after 30 free minutes, unless a French operator pays for them.
Live captions on iPhone needs iOS 26 or later, and official pages say little about it so far.
The French relay offer (sign language, LfPC, human-corrected captions) is limited to 5 hours a month, opening hours and calls within France and its overseas departments.

notes: Live captions (in-person) is new: App Store version 6.1.0, released 2026-10-26, with short help articles in English and French; not on the US or international homepages. Whether Live captions is free or uses call credit is not stated. Its languages and speaker labels are not stated. Airplane mode only on the French features page. France free hours: help centre and French site say 5 h/month since 1 October 2026; French App Store and Google Play descriptions still say 3 h (the earlier amount). Free Mobile is not an eligible operator. Languages: 100+ (international site, US/UK stores; used in text), 80+ (French store and Google Play), help-centre list dated 2021 = 119 locale entries in 64 languages (our count). Countries: help centre lists 44 download / 38 purchase / 9 incoming-call countries (used in text); international site says more than 52. Top-up: US$10.99 for 2 h (English help centre), €11.99 (French help + store), £9.99 (UK store); US store lists no top-up. Stores also list 'Halfprice' variants no official page explains. No desktop app found, though the French relay page mentions computers. rogervoice.com/en/pricing returned 404. Google Play was read with curl.
